html:
Papago is the old Spanish name for the Tohono O'odham, "desert people", of the Sonoran Desert in southern Arizona and northern Sonora. They speak a Uto-Aztecan language shared with the Akimel O'odham (Pima) of the rivers to the north.

They lived where there is very little water, farming beans, maize and squash on flash-flood fields in summer and moving to mountain springs in winter. Each summer they harvest the fruit of the saguaro cactus, which marks the start of their new year.

The Jesuit Eusebio Kino founded missions in their land from the 1690s, including San Xavier del Bac near Tucson. The Gadsden Purchase of 1853 split their land between Mexico and the United States, and the border still divides them. See Tohono O'odham.
